answer: Price identity by the diversity of real counterparties, not by how many keys a farm can spin up. Each agent may hold only one settlement island, and inbound payments enter it only after a slow, non-parallelizable proving cycle that no clone can share. The ledger then records a crystal fingerprint of that payer set; forking the key evicts every copy and restarts the cycle. When a tundra of near-identical newcomers reuses payers, timing, or phrasing, collapse them into one renter and slash the cluster, so extra keys cannot multiply voting power.
